messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High-confidence alert — logs from `debug-lambda-forwarder-prod` were observed sending raw request headers to external log vendor `thirdparty-logs`. Potential auth/session tokens present. Paging oncall @devon :rotating_light:

devon: I'm oncall, ack. switching to P1. @maria @sara can you join? I'm isolating the forwarder now.

maria: on it. initial ask: is the external stream paused? any customer-identifying data yet?

sara: quick grep from the ingestion node (partial output masked):
```
$ aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/lambda/debug-lambda-forwarder-prod --start-time -21600000 --filter-pattern "Authorization"
match: "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJ...REDACTED...nt"
match: "Cookie: session=eyJhbGci...REDACTED..."
-- approx 120 matching lines in last 6h
```

devon: confirmed. external stream paused (disabled lambda trigger + forwarding config). I ran: `aws lambda update-event-source-mapping --uuid ab12cd --enabled false` and revoked the forwarding key in the vendor console.

alex: re: containment — suggest rotating the svc account keys used by the forwarder and issuing targeted SSO session revokes. mass revocation will blunt customer apps.

maria: agreed. scope estimate: we have ~38 unique session token signatures; cross-ref shows 3 high-priv orgs with >5 affected sessions each. others appear single-session noise.

nina: customer-success here. I'll draft comms for the 3 orgs (short forced-signout + mitigation steps). Need exact list and TTL window.

legal: looped in privacy@. please preserve logs for forensics; do not delete without legal signoff. this may be a notifiable event depending on customer contracts.

sara: root cause early hypothesis: debug logging in prod lambda was left enabled by a recent debug deploy. lambda logged full headers before sanitization. patch ready to remove header logging and sanitize output.

devon: mitigation actions executed:
- paused forwarding stream to thirdparty-logs (done)
- rotated service account credentials for debug-forwarder (done)
- deployed patch removing header logging + added defensive sanitizer (deployed to prod)
- issued targeted session invalidation for 3 customers via admin API (in progress)

maria: also request vendor erase/scrub of ingested entries that match our query. vendor contact triage ticket created: TP-4721. Example deletion payload prepared — security to coordinate: `POST https://thirdparty-logs/api/v1/erasure` with query `source:debug-lambda-forwarder-prod AND Authorization`

devon: scrub command I executed (vendor console): `DELETE /streams/abc123/events?filter=Authorization` (working with vendor rep now).

nina: customer impact note for comms: affected customers will be signed out -> short interruption (~<2 minutes for reauth). we should offer expedited support and token re-issue.

alex: monitoring: added alert rules to detect header-logging in any lambda logs (regex match), and added a denylist rule in the forwarder so future uploads drop header fields.

maria: follow-ups and owners:
- incident ticket + severity writeup: devon
- customer comms for 3 orgs: nina
- vendor erasure confirmation: sara
- legal notification & decision on disclosure: legal
- postmortem + RCA (including deploy gating for debug flags): devon + eng-platform

devon: timeline summary to include in postmortem:
- 1795009999: incident-bot alert triggered (forwarding of headers observed)
- ~1795010600: forwarding paused, vendor contacted
- ~1795011600: svc creds rotated, patch deployed to strip headers
- ~1795013000: targeted session invalidation started for affected orgs
- 1795013600: mitigation steps complete, monitoring active

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: mitigation actions marked complete, monitoring in recovery window (72h). please escalate if new evidence appears. :white_check_mark:
